userDecision.summary: Do not ask the user to judge physical UI size from a small screenshot. Research real mobile-game adaptation practice, apply it to S02, keep all repository work on live kimi, and report the matching Vercel preview URL after each repository change.

rejectedApproach.name: uniform-full-screen-scaling
rejectedApproach.reason: The supported portrait viewports do not share one aspect ratio. Uniformly shrinking the complete screen would also shrink text and touch targets below readable and operable minimums. Non-uniform stretching would distort the artwork and UI chrome.

responsiveStrategy.artwork: Preserve aspect ratio and crop or reveal additional background as necessary.
responsiveStrategy.interface: Reflow and collapse secondary information by width and available height; do not scale the entire interface as a flattened image.
responsiveStrategy.extraHeight: Allocate additional height primarily to the battlefield.
responsiveStrategy.shortScreen: Retain critical text and controls, hide or move secondary explanation into the scroll flow, and allow vertical scrolling.
responsiveStrategy.safeArea: Keep critical controls inside top and bottom safe-area insets while decorative background may extend edge to edge.

researchBasis.source: Apple Human Interface Guidelines — Designing for games and UI design tips
researchBasis.finding: iOS game text should remain at least 11 pt and touch controls at least 44 by 44 pt; imagery should retain its aspect ratio.
Use a reference resolution with width/height matching or expansion; independent x/y stretching for mismatched aspect ratios is undesirable.
Resolution-independent game UI commonly scales from the viewport's shortest side and a configured curve rather than from one fixed screenshot.
Modern mobile devices vary in size, density and aspect ratio; portrait games use a base resolution, expand behavior and anchored controls.

researchBasis.source: Riot Games — Legends of Runeterra UI tooling
researchBasis.finding: The production game used platform-specific mobile text sizes, a device/aspect/notch simulator and safe-area constraints.
Interactive UI is constrained to a device-safe rectangle while backgrounds may continue to the screen edges.
